chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Musa, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The miscarried child, when four months are completed for it, is washed.
ai.seo_question: When does a miscarried fetus require ritual washing before burial?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the legal threshold for ritual washing (ghusl) of a miscarried fetus (siqat), specifying that it becomes obligatory once the fetus reaches four lunar months of gestation. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling is significant as it distinguishes the status of the fetus as a distinct entity requiring burial rites, reflecting the scholarly consensus on the timing of ensoulment or sufficient physical formation. The chain of transmission highlights the reliability of key narrators like Zurarah and al-Husayn ibn Musa, reinforcing the authenticity of this specific medical-legal criterion.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Musa, from Zurara, 
from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The miscarried child, when four months are completed for it, would be washed (prior to burial)’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Musa from Zurarah from who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
A miscarried child (fetus) after four months is given Ghusl (bath).’”
